name: Middle English

ancestors.notes: Norman French superstrate (post-1066): /v/ becomes phonemic; /dʒ/ and /ʒ/ extended; massive vocabulary influx (~10,000 French words); loss of OE inflectional endings accelerated
Old Norse Danelaw adstrate: they/their/them, sky, take, give, etc.

notes:
Middle English (~1100–1500 CE). Post-Norman Conquest (~1066); models Chaucerian Late ME (~1380–1400). NORMAN FRENCH SUPERSTRATE: /v/ phonemicised; /dʒ/ extended via French; /ʒ/ enters (vision, pleasure) in late ME. OE diphthongs simplified: ea→ɛ, eo→e. OE front rounded /y/ → /i/ (lost). GREAT VOWEL SHIFT beginning ~1400–1700: long vowels raised/diphthongised. Dialect continuum: Northern (Scots), Midland (Chaucer), Southern. Major texts: Canterbury Tales (Chaucer), Piers Plowman, Sir Gawain and the Green Knight. Source: Hogg (1992), Fischer (2000).

GOLD FORENSICS (wikipron, this pass, see docs/gold_defects.md): the wikipron enm gold's vowel-length notation does not hold still even within one headword -- counted on the harness's own scored representation (each reading normalized via benchmark.normalize(broad=True, strip_stress=True), deduplicated per headword), 1,403 of 6,466 headwords (21.7%) retain two or more distinct normalized readings that differ ONLY by the presence of the length mark ː (the same predicate over raw un-normalized TSV strings gives 1,291/20.0% instead; 1,403 is reported because it matches what the PER computation actually scores). Spot-checked mismatches (Irish -> gold iːriʃ, Simon -> gold simɔːn, amen -> gold aːmɛn) assign length to plain vowel letters with no orthographic signal this spec's macron graphemes (ā ē ī ō ū) could use to predict it. Folding ː out of both sides moves PER from the as-scored 0.2981 to 0.2538 (valid_ceiling.wikipron) -- below the 0.25 production threshold, so this row stays OPEN, not proved input-limited. Word-final -e is similarly unstable: of 2,350 headwords with an orthographic final e, 1,922 (81.8%) have SOME readings realise it as [ə] and others drop it for the SAME headword; a naive fold (strip trailing [ə] on both sides when the headword ends in e) makes PER worse (0.3144), a negative result, so no ceiling is recorded for it. Headword spelling is also not standardised: 669 of 6,465 adjacent-sorted headword pairs are plausible dialectal/scribal variants of one lexeme, a property of unstandardised ME spelling rather than a spec defect. INHERITANCE: en-GB (parent=enm) carries zero *_base keys, so nothing crosses from enm into en-GB or any further English lect; en-US instead inherits from en-GB (not enm) via four *_base keys (graphemes_base, allophones_base, grammatical_endings_base, word_exceptions_base). enm is safe to edit freely; en-GB is the shared base and is not.

wikipron.citation: As-scored PER (n=6466, broad+strip_stress, enm_latn_broad.tsv) is 0.2981, matching the committed board row. Counted on the harness's own scored representation (each reading run through benchmark.normalize(broad=True, strip_stress=True), deduplicated per headword), 1403 of the 6466 headwords (21.7%) retain two or more distinct normalized readings that differ from each other ONLY by the presence of ː on a vowel -- the gold disagrees with itself about vowel length within the same headword (Irish -> readings iriʃ / iːriʃ; Simon -> simɔn / simɔːn). The same predicate over raw, un-normalized TSV strings gives 1291 (20.0%) instead; 1403 is reported here because normalization always runs before scoring, so it is the count that matches what the PER computation actually sees. Spot-checked mismatches assign length to plain vowel letters this spec's macron graphemes (ā ē ī ō ū) have no orthographic basis to predict. Folding ː out of both hypothesis and gold measures 0.2538 -- this does NOT clear the 0.25 production threshold, so the row remains open rather than proved input-limited; something beyond vowel-length notation still accounts for roughly a quarter of the row's segments. Folding combining acute/grave/caron alongside it made no difference (0.2538, unchanged) -- the gold does not carry those marks for this row, a negative result, not a second ceiling contributor. A separate fold for word-final -e (strip trailing [ə] on both sides when the headword ends in orthographic e) was tried and makes PER worse (0.3144) because it strips correct [ə] outputs into mismatches; that is a negative result, not a ceiling -- see docs/gold_defects.md.
